label_source.evidence: The inputs of a detection system are a low-quality training set eDtrain = {(xi, eyi)}Ni=1 where N ≪|Dtest| and eyi is a noisy label that may be inconsistent with yi.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: The feature extraction module utilizes a Transformer model to convert encrypted traffic into feature vectors that capture the comprehensive behavior of the traffic

features_used.evidence: We first divide raw encrypted traffic into network flows based on the five-tuple information and use the sequence of packet lengths of each flow as the input data for feature extraction

model_family.evidence: Finally, our system utilizes a DL-based detector built upon Co-teaching [32] and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) that is trained on the synthesized and the label-corrected original training data.

split_protocols.evidence: Each size represents the number of malicious and normal training samples randomly selected from T1 in each experiment.

main_split.evidence: Each size represents the number of malicious and normal training samples randomly selected from T1 in each experiment.

metrics.evidence: We utilize three common metrics to evaluate the performance of our detection system, including precision, recall, and F1 score, which is consistent with the prior work.

granularity.evidence: We first divide raw encrypted traffic into network flows based on the five-tuple information and use the sequence of packet lengths of each flow as the input data for feature extraction

first_n_packets.evidence: We use l = [l1, l2, . . . , ln] to denote the packet length sequence of n packets in a flow, where li is the length of the i-th packet.

cost_reported.evidence: After training, our system supports low-latency and high-throughput inference, with a latency of 2ms and a throughput of over 42, 000 network flows per second, making it suitable for real-time deployment.
